primitives.name: Rigid Motion Invariance
primitives.verbatim_quote: The other two axioms peculiar to geometry are that figures can be moved in space without change, and that no variation in the way of subdividing a given amount of space alters its total quantity.\ This last axiom is similar to what we found to obtain in numbers.
primitives.assumptions: Figures maintain intrinsic properties under translation and rotation; spatial subdivision preserves total quantity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spatial warping or magnification occurs, invariance fails.

layer2.mapping: Isometric embeddings define equivalence classes of geometric forms under rigid transformations.
layer2.telemetry: Shape preservation metrics under Euclidean group action.
